title: 主旨题
goal: 听出短讲讨论的概念；排除范围过大或过小的选项。
exam: TOEFL iBT（2026 年 1 月起的新版）· 听力

points.label: 排除范围过大或过小的选项

sources.title: ETS：TOEFL iBT Test 2026 Update — Test Blueprint and Specifications

body.p: 主旨题要求概括整段短讲的中心概念和主要关系。开场的物品、地点或故事常常只是引入。概念出现之后的解释、例子和结论，共同决定主旨的范围。

body.box:
What is the talk mainly about?
What is the main point of the talk?
Which title best fits the talk?

body.p: 题干中的 mainly、main point 和 best title 都指整段内容。短讲先用建筑说明 negative space，再讲雕塑中的空隙，主旨就是空间的作用，而不只是建筑。

steps.d: 找到引入之后的定义或中心观点。This is called negative space. 之后的解释确定了概念。主旨不按第一个出现的名词来定。
用概念加主要关系来概括，不罗列所有例子。Empty areas help organize a design. 一句就能概括建筑和雕塑两个例子。
用结尾和主要解释核对选项的范围。How all buildings are designed 超出了空间这个话题。The doorway of one building 只剩下一个例子。

cards.title: 概念与范围
rows: 引入后的命名
记下定义，开场的物品多半只是例子
An empty courtyard illustrates negative space.
反复解释的关系
同一关系换说法反复出现，比同一个词重复更重要
An unfilled area can separate two visual elements.
多个例子
概括几个例子的共同作用，不超出话题
A courtyard and a gap in a sculpture both shape attention.
结论的限定
选项也要保留 can、some 这类限定
Empty areas can be part of a deliberate design.
对比内容
看讲者主要解释的是哪一方
Instead of studying the solid blocks, consider the spaces between them.
概念加关系
只写话题太宽，要写出主要观点
How unfilled areas contribute to visual design.

body.box: A sculpture isn't made only of solid material. The spaces between its parts also affect what viewers see. Artists call these unfilled areas negative space. An opening can separate two figures or make their connection more noticeable. A courtyard can play a similar role in a building. This doesn't mean empty areas are always intentional. But when they are planned, the absence of material becomes part of the design.

What is the talk mainly about?
1. How courtyards are added to buildings
2. Why sculptures require solid materials
3. How unfilled areas contribute to a design
4. Why every empty area has an artistic purpose

body.p: 概念是 negative space，主要关系是未填充的区域影响设计。第三项同时涵盖雕塑和庭院。contribute to a design 概括了 affect what viewers see 和结尾的 part of the design。
第一项只取了庭院这个例子。第二项把用来对比的实体材料当成了主旨。第四项把 when they are planned 扩大成了 every。

cards.title: 干扰项
rows: 范围过小
The openings in a particular sculpture
只讲雕塑，漏了建筑和共同的概念
范围过大
The purposes of every part of a building
扩大到建筑的全部构件，超出了空隙的作用
对比内容
The importance of solid materials alone
原文从实体转到空隙，重点在空隙
程度过强
Every empty area is intentionally designed
与 doesn't mean … always intentional 相反

lines.text: A glacier isn't the only way ice moves. Today the focus is sea ice drifting under wind and ocean currents. Unlike a glacier, sea ice forms from seawater and floats. Its movement reflects conditions in the surrounding air and water.

items.stem: What is the short talk mainly about?
options: How floating sea ice differs from a glacier
Why ice forms from seawater near a coast
How ocean currents change with wind direction
How wind and currents move floating sea ice
items.why: 依据是 the focus is sea ice drifting under wind and ocean currents。第四项说的就是风和洋流推动海冰，glacier 只是对比的对象。

lines.text: A woven basket can flex because its strips move slightly against one another. The material matters, but so does the way the strips cross. Today we're considering how weaving creates a structure that bends without immediately coming apart.

items.stem: Which title best matches the scope?
options: How Interlaced Strips Give Baskets Flexibility
How Basket Materials Are Selected and Prepared
How Individual Strips Resist Coming Apart
Why Material Choice Alone Determines Basket Flexibility
items.why: 依据是 how weaving creates a structure that bends。第一项同时包含交织和柔韧这两点。第四项把材料说成唯一的原因，与 so does the way the strips cross 不符。

lines.text: A word can keep its form while its meaning changes. For instance, a term once used for a physical tool may later name a computer function. Such changes show how existing vocabulary is adapted to new uses, rather than replaced entirely.

items.stem: Which concept is the speaker explaining?
options: The replacement of older words by computer terminology
The influence of physical tools on computer design
Changes in the meanings of existing words over time
Differences between technical words and everyday words
items.why: 依据是 a word can keep its form while its meaning changes。第三项改写了 meaning changes，范围也是 existing vocabulary。第一项的 replacement 与 rather than replaced entirely 相反。

lines.text: A river bend often has faster flow near its outer bank and slower flow near its inner bank. This contrast helps explain erosion on one side and deposition on the other. The subject is how unequal flow shapes a bend, not how all river valleys begin.

items.stem: Which title is neither too broad nor too narrow?
options: All Processes That Create River Valleys
How Unequal Flow Shapes River Bends
Deposition Along a Single Inner Bank
Why Faster Flow Deposits Material on Outer Banks
items.why: 依据是 how unequal flow shapes a bend，它包含两岸的变化，即第二项。第四项把外岸的侵蚀说成了沉积。

lines.text: Consider two versions of the same melody. A flute and a violin can play the same note, yet they don't sound identical. The difference illustrates timbre, the quality that helps distinguish sounds even when pitch and loudness are similar. Each instrument produces a different combination of vibrations, and the beginning of a note can also differ. A violin bow may sustain a sound while a plucked string quickly fades. Pitch tells us how high or low a note is; timbre helps explain its character. So identifying an instrument by ear involves more than recognizing the note it plays.

items.stem: What is the talk mainly about?
options: How loudness distinguishes instruments playing a melody
How pitch identifies the instrument producing a note
How plucking and bowing change a string's duration
Why sounds at similar pitches can have different qualities
items.why: 依据是定义 timbre, the quality that helps distinguish sounds even when pitch and loudness are similar。音高相近，音色仍可不同，即第四项。

items.stem: Which proposed title covers only one supporting example?
options: The Different Qualities of Musical Sounds
How a Plucked String Fades
Distinguishing Instruments by Their Sound
Timbre Beyond Pitch and Loudness
items.why: a plucked string quickly fades 只是说明音色的一个例子。第二项只覆盖了这一处，其他标题讲的都是整体概念。

lines.text: A burr attached to a jacket may seem like an inconvenience, but it illustrates a way plants move their seeds. Today's subject is seed dispersal: the movement of seeds away from the plant that produced them. A seed doesn't walk, yet its structure can make movement possible. Some seeds have hooks that catch on an animal's fur. Others have light surfaces that allow the wind to carry them. Animals may also eat a fruit and later leave its seeds in another place. These methods don't guarantee that a seed reaches suitable ground. A seed carried far away may land where it cannot grow. Still, movement can reduce the crowding that would occur if all the seeds remained directly beneath the parent plant. It can also bring seeds to newly available places. The important connection is between a seed's form, the agent that carries it, and the opportunity to establish a new plant elsewhere. The burr is one example of that connection, rather than the whole subject. Dispersal creates opportunities for growth; it doesn't ensure successful growth in every destination.

items.stem: What is the talk mainly about?
options: How seed structures and carriers enable movement to new places
How fruit protects seeds while they grow beneath a plant
Why wind carries seeds farther than animals do
Why seeds need to remain close to parent plants
items.why: 依据是定义 seed dispersal: the movement of seeds away from the plant that produced them，后文又把 form 和 agent 联系起来。第一项概括了这层关系。

items.stem: Which title covers only a supporting detail?
options: The Movement of Seeds Beyond the Parent Plant
Different Ways for Seeds to Reach New Locations
Hooks That Attach Seeds to Animal Fur
Seed Movement and Opportunities for New Growth
items.why: Some seeds have hooks that catch on an animal's fur 只是多种传播方式中的一种。第三项漏掉了风力和动物吃果实这两种方式。

items.stem: Which title adds a claim beyond the talk's scope?
options: Seed Carriers and the Shapes That Assist Them
Seed Dispersal as a Guarantee of Successful Growth
How Movement Reduces Crowding Near Parent Plants
Different Routes by Which Seeds Reach Other Places
items.why: 依据是 These methods don't guarantee that a seed reaches suitable ground。第二项把机会说成了保证。第三项范围较窄，但原文有依据。

lines.text: Imagine a building assembled from sections made in a factory. This is an example of modular construction, where repeated units are produced separately and then joined at the site. The focus isn't the appearance of one particular building. It's how dividing a project into units changes the building process. While workers prepare the site, a factory can make the units. Some work can therefore happen at the same time instead of waiting for an earlier stage to finish. Repetition may also make it easier to check whether units meet the same standard. However, the joins require careful planning. A small mismatch can become a serious problem when large completed sections arrive. Transport also places limits on the size of a unit. Building entirely at the site offers more flexibility for changes during construction, so factory production isn't automatically preferable for every project. Modular construction reorganizes where and when work occurs. Its value depends on whether the repeated units, transport arrangements, and final connections fit the project's needs. The method offers possible efficiencies together with specific coordination demands.

options: Designing repeated units to standardize building appearance
Choosing unit dimensions primarily to simplify transportation
Revising completed units to accommodate changes at the site
Building with separately produced units that are joined on site
items.why: 依据是 modular construction, where repeated units are produced separately and then joined at the site。第四项是这句的同义概括。

items.stem: Which proposed title is too narrow for the whole talk?
options: Modular Construction: Production and Coordination
The Transport Size of a Factory-Made Unit
Benefits and Limits of Building with Repeated Units
How Modular Construction Reorganizes Building Work
items.why: Transport also places limits on the size of a unit 只是一项限制。第二项没有涵盖同步施工、标准检查和连接规划。

items.stem: What main point does the speaker make?
options: Separately made units can improve the process but require coordination.
Factory standards make the final connections less demanding to plan.
Construction at the site provides less flexibility than finished factory units.
Transportation advantages account for the method's main construction savings.
items.why: 依据是结论 possible efficiencies together with specific coordination demands。第一项同时保留了收益和协调的要求。
